title: Kea Terms of Use
summary: First version of the Kea terms.

sections.title: 1. What Kea and KeaS are
sections.body:
Kea is a free app for school, study and documents. KeaS is a free app for workplaces: scheduling, availability, time clock, certifications, classes and payroll preparation. Both use one Kea account.
The Kea Hub is the server that keeps Kea accounts, classes, study progress, leaderboards and the files you choose to store there. It is run by Kaden Walsh ("the developer", "I"), the creator of Kea, on his own computer.
These terms cover your Kea account, the Kea Hub, and the official Kea and KeaS apps. You must agree to all of them to use a Kea account.

sections.title: 2. Your account
sections.body:
- You must be 13 or older to have a Kea account.
- One account per person. Use your real email address. Don't share your account or sign in as someone else.
- Your password is never stored. The Hub keeps only a one-way scrambled form of it (a slow, memory-hard hash: Argon2id or scrypt), so nobody, including the developer, can read it. If you forget it, you reset it; it can't be looked up.
- Repeated wrong sign-ins lock the account for a growing amount of time. This protects you from people guessing your password.
- You can turn on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app. Owners of organizations, payroll admins and verified instructors must use it.
- "Verify with Google" proves you own your email: Google tells the Hub your email address and nothing else. Kea never sees your Google password.
- You are responsible for what happens under your account. Tell the developer right away if you think someone else got into it.

sections.title: 3. Use the official software only
sections.body:
- You may only connect to the Kea Hub and Kea services with the official Kea and KeaS apps, downloaded from the developer's official releases, and only while you have agreed to the current version of these terms.
- Kea's code is open source, so other people can copy and change it. A copied or modified version is not Kea. It is not made, checked or supported by the developer, even if it uses the Kea name or looks the same.
- The developer is not responsible or liable for anything a modified, unofficial or tampered version does, including one changed to skip these terms, skip safety checks (such as payroll's "verified tables" check), cheat on scores, or take your data. If you use one, you do so entirely at your own risk.
- Using a modified version to connect to the Kea Hub, or any tool that gets around the Hub's sign-in, limits or checks, breaks these terms, and the account can be suspended.

sections.title: 4. The Kea Hub runs on a personal computer
sections.body:
- The Hub runs on the developer's own computer and home internet, reached through a secure tunnel. It is not a data center.
- It can be offline: for updates, power or internet outages, or repairs. There is no guaranteed uptime. The apps keep working offline where they can, and catch up when the Hub is back.
- Live class video is not sent through the Hub. Classes use meeting links (for example Jitsi Meet, Google Meet or Zoom), which follow those services' own terms.
- Organizations that need guaranteed uptime can run their own KeaS server.

sections.title: 5. What the Hub stores, and why
6. Your Kea storage
sections.body:
- Your account comes with storage space on the Hub for your Kea data (documents, notes, study sets, settings), so your devices can stay in step without another cloud drive.
- Each account has a storage limit. The developer can change limits, and will tell you before lowering one below what you're already using.
- Your files are stored on the Hub's drives. They are protected by your sign-in and the Hub's security, but they are not end-to-end encrypted, so the Hub's operator could technically open them. The developer doesn't look at your files except when needed for security, a legal requirement, or a report of abuse.
- Keep your own copies of anything important. The Hub is backed up, but it is not a guaranteed archive.
- Don't store illegal content or other people's private information without permission. Content like that can be removed and the account suspended.

sections.title: 7. Classes, instructors and hosting
sections.body:
- Anyone can join a class with an invite code from its instructor.
- Hosting a class on the Kea Hub needs the developer's approval. Instructors can also host classes on their own organization's server without that approval.
- Publishing a general curriculum (a public class anyone can find) needs an identity-verified account, and each one is reviewed before it is listed.
- Instructors are responsible for their class content: that it's accurate, that they have the right to share it, and that it's appropriate for their students. Don't upload publishers' test banks, scanned textbooks or other material you don't have rights to.
- Classes in Kea don't replace official certification. A certificate from an organization (for example a lifeguarding or CPR card) comes from that organization or the certifying agency, not from Kea.
- The developer can remove a class or take away hosting at any time, especially to protect students.

sections.title: 8. Study tools, scores and leaderboards
sections.body:
How scoring works:
- A question earns points only when it is due: new, or back for review.
- Right on the first try earns the most. Right after a wrong answer still earns a little, so practicing until you get it counts. Wrong answers never cost points.
- Answering a question again before it is due is free practice and earns nothing.
- Questions come back on a spaced schedule (1 day, then 3, 7, 14 days and longer) so you remember them.
- There is a daily point limit.
- Answers are checked by the Hub, so scores can't be changed by editing the app.
Leaderboards:
- In each class you choose how you appear: your name, a nickname, or hidden. Hidden people still see their own rank.
- Scores and levels are for motivation. They are not grades and not an official academic record.
- Using bots, scripts, shared answer keys or extra accounts to raise scores breaks these terms; the scores can be removed and the account suspended.

sections.title: 9. Organizations and workplaces
sections.body:
- An organization (for example an employer, club or school) can use KeaS for schedules, availability forms, time clock, certifications, classes and payroll preparation. You join one with its code.
- The organization decides what it collects about its members and is responsible for that data (it is the "data controller"). Questions or deletion requests about an organization's records go to that organization.
- Org admins can see what their organization needs to run: for example your availability, schedule, hours and the certifications you choose to share with them.
- Schedules drafted automatically (with or without AI) are suggestions until a manager publishes them.
- KeaS is a tool. The organization is responsible for following labor law, paying people correctly, and keeping its official records.

sections.title: 10. Payroll
sections.body:
- KeaS calculates pay, withholding and employer taxes, makes pay stubs, direct-deposit files and pre-filled forms. The employer reviews them, submits filings and pays taxes. The employer is always the employer of record and stays legally responsible for payroll, whatever software it uses.
- KeaS never holds, moves or receives money, and never files taxes for anyone. If an organization connects its own bank, payments go straight from the organization's own account.
- Tax and labor tables are only marked "verified for <year>" after they are checked against official sources. KeaS won't finalize a pay run on unverified tables, and you must not use a version of KeaS that skips this check.
- Check every pay run. Run the first ones alongside another calculator, and consider having an accountant review your first year.
- Nothing in Kea or KeaS is tax, legal or financial advice.

sections.title: 11. Claude and other AI features
sections.body:
- AI features are optional, except researching or updating tax and labor tables in KeaS, which needs Claude. Everything else can be done by hand.
- AI features use your own Claude account, under Anthropic's terms, unless you use Kea's shared Claude (section 11b). Kea sends Claude only what the feature needs.
- AI output can be wrong. It is a draft (a schedule, a lesson, a table change, an explanation) until a person reviews it. Nothing an AI makes is published, sent or used for pay on its own.

sections.title: 11b. Kea's shared Claude
sections.body:
If you don't have your own Claude, the developer's Claude can do a limited amount of work for you, for free, in a queue. To keep it working for everyone:
- You need a verified email.
- Each of your classes gets one first scan, and updates when something new is posted. If someone in your course section was already scanned, you share theirs right away.
- When you run out of practice questions, you can ask for 25 more for a chapter, a few times per chapter. Classes are never regenerated from scratch on the shared Claude.
- There are daily and weekly limits, and requests wait in line and run one at a time. Wait times can be long, and the queue can be paused.
- Material made from a shared scan is shared with others in the same course section. Your grades, your own assignments and your private work are never shared.
- Sending requests automatically, using several accounts to get around the limits, or overloading the queue gets the account suspended for review.
- The shared Claude is a free extra, not a guaranteed service. It can change or stop at any time. For more, connect your own Claude.

sections.title: 12. What you must not do
sections.body:
- Try to break into the Hub or anyone's account, guess passwords, get around limits, or test security without the developer's written permission.
- Overload the Hub, scrape it, or use automated tools against it.
- Harass, threaten or bully anyone, or share someone's private information.
- Pretend to be someone else, or to be verified when you're not.
- Upload illegal content, malware, or material you don't have the rights to.
- Use Kea to put minors at risk in any way. This is reported to the authorities.

sections.title: 13. Members under 18
sections.body:
- Members aged 13 to 17 can use Kea. Their leaderboard and profile settings start private.
- Organizations employing minors are responsible for minor-labor rules and any parent notices.
- A parent or guardian can ask the developer to delete a minor's account.

sections.title: 14. Other services
sections.body: Kea can connect to services run by others: Google, Microsoft, Anthropic (Claude), meeting services, school sites, banks, and the tunnel service that carries Hub traffic (Tailscale or Cloudflare). Those services have their own terms and privacy policies, and the developer isn't responsible for them.

sections.title: 14b. Donations
sections.body:
- Kea is free. You can chip in through the "Support Kea" link if you want to, and Kea never asks you again or locks anything behind it.
- Donations are gifts that help pay for running Kea. They don't buy extra shared-Claude use, priority, features or any promise of service, and they aren't refundable unless the law requires it.

sections.title: 15. No warranty
sections.body: Kea, KeaS and the Kea Hub are provided free and "as is", without warranties of any kind, including that they will be accurate, available, secure or fit for a particular purpose, to the fullest extent the law allows.

sections.title: 16. Limits on liability
sections.body:
- To the fullest extent the law allows, the developer is not liable for indirect, incidental or consequential losses, lost data, lost profits, penalties or fines, including tax penalties from payroll errors.
- The developer's total liability for any claim about Kea is limited to the greater of what you paid for Kea in the 12 months before the claim (Kea is free, so usually nothing) or 50 US dollars.
- The developer is never liable for unofficial or modified versions (section 3), for organizations' decisions, or for content made by instructors or other members.

sections.title: 17. Suspension and closing your account
sections.body:
- You can stop using Kea and ask to delete your account at any time. You can also download your data.
- The developer can suspend or close an account that breaks these terms or puts others at risk, and will explain why when it's safe to.
- Sections 3, 15, 16 and 19 still apply after an account is closed.

sections.title: 18. When these terms change
sections.body:
- Each version of these terms is numbered and dated, and old versions stay readable.
- When the terms change, the apps show you exactly which sections were added, changed or removed.
- You must agree to the new version before your account can use the Kea Hub again. Until then you can still read the terms, download your data, and sign out.
- If you don't agree, don't keep using Kea. You can ask for your account to be deleted.

sections.title: 19. Law and contact
sections.body:
- These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Colorado, USA, and disputes go to the courts there, unless the law where you live says otherwise.
- If part of these terms can't be enforced, the rest still applies.
- Contact: use "Contact Kea" in the app.
